raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate marked tracheomegaly (dilated trachea) and extensive bilateral cystic bronchiectasis with multiple large cavities, which are hallmark features of Mounier-Kuhn Syndrome. The progression to increased cavity size and number indicates disease advancement, necessitating management focused on airway clearance (physiotherapy) and treating superimposed infections with antibiotics.
